messages:
incident-bot: Pager: hosted-runtime kv-cache memory climb detected on shard set rgx-3. auto-threshold (85%) breached, potential OOM if sustained. tags: kv-cache, continuous-batching, hosted, prod. ops runbook link: https://redwood.internal/ops/kv-cache-runaway

Evan: I'm oncall, looking now. seeing mem climb on multiple hosts in rgx-3, recent spike started ~1769998800. p95 latency up ~200ms, error rate to customers ~0.6% but some 503s.

Sam: thanks Evan. quick ask — any recent rollout to batching or prefetch configs in us-west?

Priya: I pushed a batching config change ~1769998600 for continuous-batching: max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 to try to reduce per-token amortized overhead. I can roll back if that's the culprit.

Evan: that aligns. graphs show batch token counts jumped ~2.1x since 1769998600. Also kv-cache entries exploded — cardinality up on prefix keys. looks like long prompt sessions are causing massive prefix growth and prefetches.

Jules: is this the same as the earlier runaway-window issues? could be related, but the shape is different — we see many unique key prefixes per session instead of repeated long tails.

Maya-CS: CS reports 3 customers with elevated 5xxs for generation endpoints (hosted-high). priority customers A & B affected minimally but please flag once we know ETA.

Evan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce continuous-batching max_batch_tokens back to 4096 (rollback), 2) enable prefetch session cap at 8 for hosted runtime, 3) tighten kv-cache prefetch window to 1024 tokens for incoming long prompts, 4) trigger per-host eviction sweep. will coordinate.

Priya: rollback command ready. deploy-bot, can we push config rollback to rgx-3 only?

deploy-bot: @Priya config rollback pipeline queued: rollback continuous-batching.max_batch_tokens -> 4096 for service hosted-runtime/rgx-3. Dry-run passes. ETA 90s to stage, 180s to mat.

Evan: I'm going to throttle prefetch at the proxy layer to reduce fanout. command: 
```
# reduce prefetch workers
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/rgx-3/config -d '{"kv_prefetch_workers":2}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

infra-sre: prefetch worker change applied to 50% of nodes in rgx-3 (canary). observing drop in outbound prefetch calls already.

Sam: we're also seeing large multi-part prompts from a batch of sessions that generate unique context keys per turn — prefix-cardinality explosion. Suggest adding immediate TTL on keys created by sessions older than 10m.

Priya: can add a short TTL at the cache layer for newly created session prefixes. patch ready: set session_prefix_ttl_seconds=600. Will push to rgx-3 after rollback completes.

Evan: Agree. Priority order: rollback batching -> throttle prefetch -> set TTL -> eviction sweep. We'll keep canaries then full.

deploy-bot: continuous-batching rollback to 4096 applied to rgx-3 canary (10% nodes) at 1769998920. Observability: batch sizes decreased on canary, mem growth slowed on those nodes.

Maya-CS: customer A reports fewer failures since ~1769998930. thanks team.

Jules: pushing TTL and prefetch cap now. patch applied to canary at 1769998960. session_prefix_ttl_seconds=600, session_prefetch_cap=8.

infra-sre: eviction sweep started on canary hosts: force-evict keys with last_access_time < now-600s and key_length>2048. logs: 
```
[1769998965] evict_runner: evicted 12.3M keys, reclaimed 18.2GB on node host-21
[1769998966] evict_runner: evicted 11.4M keys, reclaimed 17.1GB on node host-22
```

Evan: nice. mem usage on canary nodes back below 60% and p95 latency trending down. rolling to 50% now.

Priya: rolling full rollback and TTL across rgx-3 in 30s.

deploy-bot: rollback + TTL + prefetch_cap rollout initiated at 1769998988 target: rgx-3 all nodes. expected full completion ~1769999028.

Sam: note for postmortem — the batching change increased batch aggregation horizon; combined with user agent generating high-variability long prompts -> high prefix cardinality -> prefetch fanout amplified. Need safe-guard: autoscaling of batch horizon only after cardinality analysis and prefetch caps.

Maya-CS: Status update for customers: Affected customers reduced to intermittent with degraded latency only. No data loss. CS will send a brief comms to priority accounts noting brief impact and corrective actions.

Evan: rolling completed at canary then full, confirming final metrics: mem 58% median across rgx-3, p95 latency back to normal, error rate <0.1%. Last impacted 5xx spikes at 1769998945.

Jules: recommend follow-ups: 1) add preflight check to config pipeline to detect broad increases in unique key cardinality when raising max_batch_tokens, 2) instrument per-session prefix-growth metric and alert on slope > X/min, 3) run a chaos test simulating long prompt cardinality.

Priya: ack. I'll open PRs for: preflight checks + TTL default + safer batch-horizon autoscaling.

Evan: handing off to next oncall @Sam for follow-up. Sam, take it from here.

Sam: taking handoff. Will create incident ticket and assign owners. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042 (kv-cache-cardinality-burst-hosted) severity: high -> mitigated. Links: runbook, graphs, incident ticket https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042
